system.name: TRACE
system.one_liner: Prompting method that has an MLLM write a structured text scene description (meta context, trajectory, entities) before answering spatial questions on egocentric video.

content.variant_note: one office scene shown as video frames with a question, as a person's description plus a top-down map, and as the TRACE text; matching colours tie the three forms together
content.argues: Humans reason about a room via an allocentric layout that text can describe; TRACE gives MLLMs the same kind of structured text trace (meta context, trajectory, entity registry).
content.subject: One office scene as video with a spatial question, a person's text-plus-map description, and TRACE's structured text.

style.stroke: 1.25 pt coloured outlines (60% opaque) on the three rounded panel frames and the braces; about 0.6 pt outlines on the map parts; black film strip

encoding.color_means: Object colours link the three views: trash can green, desk pink, telephone lavender, cup light blue, whiteboard grey; north indigo, west yellow; room blue; the three camera steps light, mid and dark orange (braces, cones, step labels). The panel tints pink, purple and amber only separate the panels.
encoding.line_style_means: solid coloured rounded frames bound the panels; curly braces in graded orange group each passage; the film-strip border says video; the red solid and green dotted arrows on the map are the viewer's right and front axes.
encoding.shape_means: film strip = video input; tinted rounded frame = panel; cone = camera pose; coloured disc or rectangle = object; brace pair = one camera pose in the text.
encoding.marker_means: (a)(b)(c) letters head the panels; step0 and step1 order the camera steps; ids such as trash_can_01 name entities; front, right, N and W name axes on the map.
encoding.emphasis: The method panel is the tallest and comes last; the multicoloured object names that recur in (b), the map and (c) draw the eye to the correspondence, while the method itself carries no extra highlight.
reusable_patterns: same colour for the same object in a human description, a map and a structured record

lessons.what_to_learn: Carry one concrete scene through every panel and give each object a fixed colour that reappears in the human description, the map and the structured record, so the correspondence reads without arrows. End with the method as a prompt card whose slots keep those colours.
lessons.suits: Motivation figures for methods that turn a raw modality (video, 3D scene, table) into structured text, where one worked scene makes the abstraction concrete.

evidence: such allocentric representations can be vividly described using text alone, as demonstrated in Fig. 1(b)
TRACE encodes meta-context, camera trajectory, and entities, serving as an intermediate reasoning trace for spatial QA with MLLMs.
Meta Context describing the room layout and coordinate system, camera Trajectory sampled over temporal windows

summary: TRACE (Textual Representation of Allocentric Context from Egocentric Video) is a prompting method that has a multimodal LLM write a structured text description of a 3D scene before answering a spatial question about egocentric video. Figure 1 motivates it with one office scene shown three ways. Panel (a) poses a quadrant question over a film strip of three video frames. Panel (b) shows how a person would describe the room in three short passages next to a top-down map with a desk, trash can, phone, cup and camera cones. Panel (c) shows the TRACE prompt and its sections: Meta Context, Trajectory and Entity Registry. Object names keep the same colour across (b), the map and (c), and three orange shades link the camera steps. The panels are pastel rounded frames with captions below.
summary_zh: TRACE 动机图：同一办公室场景分三个面板——(a) 空间提问加三帧视频胶片，(b) 人的房间文字描述加俯视图，(c) TRACE 的结构化文本（元上下文、轨迹、实体登记）。物体在三处用同一颜色对应，不画箭头。
notes: The prior pass listed concept-schematic (analogy) first; worked-walkthrough is first here because one scene with real values runs through all panels and the human-insight panel is an analogue inside it. The colour correspondences (objects, compass letters, three orange shades for brace pairs, cones and step labels) are read from the figure and its SVG, not stated in the caption. The paper text provided does not say what the green 'front-right' and red 'Cartesian Plane' spans in the question mean. The caption icons are tiny; the head-and-bulb reading of the (b) icon is a guess. The map's desk, phone, cup and trash-can discs are small masked bitmaps; cones, door, window and room outline are vector.
